learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 2 and locked the fewest bidder count prediction for a second price auction beating the best price tag with random values from $0 to $100.
observations.exploration: Initial one bidder showed tag $25 and auction $0. At two bidders, tag $38.49 beat auction $33.33. At three, auction $50 beat tag $47.25. Simulated 1,000 three bidder sales: tag $45.93 and auction $50.30. At four bidders, auction $60 beat tag $53.50.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to three and accurately compared the two and three bidder cases. It explained the tradeoff in choosing a fixed price and that a no reserve second price auction uses the second highest bid, which improves with more rivals.
observations.visual: Inspected the dark 1257 by 936 inline screenshot after the three bidder simulation. A mint best tag line and dashed white auction line crossed between two and three bidders. Numeric revenues and optimal tag prices were labelled, with simulation outcomes below.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The prompt challenges the belief that competition immediately dominates a price tag.
prediction.evidence: Selected two bidders before comparing revenue curves.

interaction.reason: Bidder counts expose a crossover, and simulation distinguishes expectation from one sample.
interaction.evidence: Tag won at two, auction won at three and four; 1,000 sales differed slightly from expected values.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the crossover using how prices are set.
payoff.evidence: It names the second highest bidder and fixed price tradeoff.

clarity.reason: The graph makes the winner change visible with explicit values.
clarity.evidence: Two labelled lines crossed between the two and three bidder results.

transfer.reason: The mechanism is explained but no new selling case or distribution is applied.
transfer.evidence: The lesson stays within the fixed random value model.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Two bidders are insufficient for the no reserve auction to beat the best tag.
surprise.evidence: $33.33 auction revenue was below $38.49 at two bidders.

visualExplanation.reason: Revenue curves communicate both the crossover and growing advantage.
visualExplanation.evidence: The lines change ordering between bidder counts two and three.

playfulness.reason: Adding bidders and simulating sales supports controlled experimentation.
playfulness.evidence: Three count buttons and one simulation button drive the model.

practicalValue.reason: It shows why a selling method depends on competition and assumptions.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal specifies no reserve and second price rules.

depth.reason: It combines expected revenue, an optimal tag and sample variation.
depth.evidence: The simulation did not exactly match the theoretical curve.

complexity.reason: Revenue comparison is straightforward, while auction rules and optimal price choice are new.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: understand how fixed price and second highest bid generate revenue differently.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: bidder count buttons and a simulation action.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Competition must become strong enough to overcome the fixed price's advantage.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Second price auctions, reserves and expected revenue are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: two revenue series, tag prices and simulation values share the chart.

whyCool: An auction's advantage appears only after enough rivals arrive, so the crossover can be watched directly.
caveat: The value model and no reserve rule are fixed. This walkthrough does not establish the best selling method for a real item.
missingEvidence: No alternative value distribution or reserve price was tested.
